quotes.text: MIMIC-IV version 2.2 (snapshot released in January 2023, hosted on PhysioNet)
every task record stores the identifier of its source patient record

rationale: The packet names the dataset, version, snapshot release date, and platform. It also states a task-to-source-record route via stored source patient identifiers.

quotes.text: approved under a data use agreement requiring credentialed access and de-identification by the safe harbour method

rationale: The evidence states the records are real de-identified hospital records and documents governance. It includes DUA, credentialed access, de-identification method, and separate data terms.

quotes.text: against the U.S. adult inpatient population reported in a national hospital discharge survey

rationale: Representativeness is analyzed against a named target population. The comparison includes age, sex and race distributions.

contradiction_quotes.text: safety test suite that measures unsafe outputs
a separate bias test that compares agent accuracy across patient demographic groups

rationale: searched: S1-S5. The only safety-test and bias-test evidence appears in S4 code comments, which do not count as reporting for this item under G1a. S4 suggests the opposite of the reported absence, so a contradiction flag is set.

quotes.text: Contamination mitigation includes gating access to the test split.
zero exact matches between test tasks and public sources

rationale: The paper reports developer-side gating of the test split. It also reports a measured verbatim-overlap check against public web corpora.

quotes.text: has no network path from the agent sandbox
they are not published in the repository

contradiction_quotes.text: It could therefore read the answer key in `/var/lib/caa`.

rationale: S1 states run-time isolation and names mechanisms: separate evaluation service, no network path, and unpublished labels. S2 reports a caveat for Harbor 0.1.44 where the agent could read the answer key, so the reported score is retained with contradiction flagged.

quotes.text: database snapshot, software image, and patient-simulation LLM are each version-pinned
only the model under test is called; no other external services are involved

contradiction_quotes.text: The patient simulator (inside each task container) and the must-ask judge (in the verifier) call an LLM.

rationale: S1 reports the data, software image, and patient-simulation LLM are pinned and no external services are used except the model under test. S2 describes live LLM calls for patient and judge through a host proxy, so the contradiction flag is set.

quotes.text: we ran a scripted reference solution for each task through the grader

rationale: The paper reports scripted reference solutions run through the grader. It also reports all 120 reference solutions were graded correct.

quotes.text: checks both the intended state changes and that all other records remain unchanged

rationale: Tasks include write actions that change encounter state, so NA does not apply. The packet states the grader checks both intended changes and unchanged records.

quotes.text: a random agent scores 2.5% on the same tasks

rationale: An empirical random-agent success rate is reported. This directly satisfies the anchor for trivial success being unlikely.

quotes.text: A do-nothing agent that issues no actions scores 0.0% on all 120 tasks

rationale: A do-nothing result is reported, but for 120 tasks rather than the full 333-task benchmark. This supports partial credit.

quotes.text: agreement was 94%, with a false-positive rate of 3% and a false-negative rate of 8%

rationale: The automatic evaluator was validated on benchmark outputs labelled by two physicians. Agreement and error rates are reported.

quotes.text: five independent runs per task employed separate random seeds at temperature 0.7

contradiction_quotes.text: five independent runs per task employed separate random seeds at temperature 0.7
All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times

rationale: S1 reports a repeated-run policy, separate random seeds, and temperature. S4 states a conflicting run count and sampling policy, so contradiction is flagged.

quotes.text: test the difference between the two best models with a paired permutation test (p = 0.02)

rationale: The paper reports confidence intervals for scores and a paired permutation test for the top-model comparison. This meets the headline comparison anchor.

quotes.text: five independent runs per task employed separate random seeds at temperature 0.7

contradiction_quotes.text: five independent runs per task employed separate random seeds at temperature 0.7
temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times

rationale: S1 reports the number of runs, separate seeds and temperature, and independence. S4 conflicts with the stated run count and sampling policy, so contradiction is flagged.

quotes.text: 95% bootstrap CIs where the resampling unit is the task
resamples patients to address within-patient clustering

rationale: Headline scores include bootstrap CIs. The resampling unit is named, and within-patient clustering is explicitly addressed.

quotes.text: each task executed eight times
pass^8 (share of tasks solved in all 8 runs)

rationale: The packet reports eight reruns per task. It includes a pass^8 all-runs metric and final environment-state agreement rates.

quotes.text: snapshot identifiers gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022
temperature 0 and a maximum of 2,048 output tokens
all reported numbers correspond to harness release v1.2.0

rationale: The appendix reports snapshot identifiers, decoding parameters, and harness release. Although not every table model has a snapshot ID, all three requested element types are present.

quotes.text: returns their names, descriptions, and JSON parameter schemas
Read tools consult the available clinical database
may return not_available

rationale: The benchmark defines a tool interface, so NA does not apply. S1 reports JSON schemas, read/write side effects, and return/error semantics, but the packet has no S5 chunks to determine whether side-effect disclosure reaches the agent.

quotes.text: Conformance testing confirms tool behavior matches documentation.
Two tools consist of simulated stubs providing fixed placeholder responses.

rationale: The packet reports conformance testing and discloses simulated stub behavior. Full credit requires evidence that this disclosure reaches S5 when simulation exists, but no S5 chunks are present.

quotes.text: Writes are executed against a sandboxed copy of the record
unnecessary or unsafe writes are penalised in the score
The agent prompt states that writes are sandboxed.

rationale: Write actions are applicable because clinical orders, notes, and messages can mutate state. S1 lists the write-action category, states execution is sandboxed, and says unsafe or unnecessary writes are penalised; it also says the sandboxing disclosure reaches the agent prompt.

quotes.text: The grader takes the final environment state as its input.
false-accept rate of 1% and a false-reject rate of 2%

rationale: The grader input is named as final environment state, so no non-state rationale is needed. The grader is validated on injected correct and incorrect outcomes with per-class error rates.

quotes.text: Agents have no web access during runs
A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces
every released task carries a canary string

rationale: The packet reports controls on web and retrieval leakage. It also reports a private held-out split with hidden labels and canary strings on released tasks.

quotes.text: accuracy per task family
per patient subgroup by sex and race
each table lists the number of cases in every slice

rationale: The paper reports results per task family and per patient subgroup. It also states that slice sizes are listed for every slice.

quotes.text: real de-identified records from a hospital database
de-identification by the safe harbour method
released under terms separate from the MIT code licence

rationale: The source is stated as real de-identified hospital records. Governance includes DUA, credentialed access, and safe-harbour de-identification, and data terms are separate from the code licence.
